what: LM-PANELS (2026-10-18): the 1,000-step language-model run at four threads with BF16-KERN and BF16-PANELS-1 -- LM-PAIRED's five seeds (20261011, 1001, 2002, 3003, 4004), three arms a seed in one session, their order rotated seed by seed: BCIR under bf16+exp+reduce+attn on 5804ad5 (bcir-panels: BF16-KERN's AMX kernel and BF16-PANELS-1's SwiGLU panels) and on d5bc457 (bcir-base: LM-ATTN's bcir-bf16-attn arm, before them), and torch.compile with fused AdamW under torch.autocast(cpu, bfloat16) (LM-BF16's faster PyTorch bf16 arm). The analysis was fixed before the runs (paired_panels.py's docstring): per pair of arms the ratio of the median warm steps per seed, their geometric mean and a 95% Student-t interval on the log ratios, and a +-0.01-nat margin on the test cross-entropy difference for every pair; whether the two BCIR arms end in one state seed for seed, and whether both end in LM-ATTN's bcir-bf16-attn states.
host: 4-vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz container (family 6 model 207: AMX-BF16 and AVX512-BF16; the instance of ../ and ../../attnfma/lm/), GCC 13.3 (the trainer builds), PyTorch 2.13.0 at four intra-op threads, Python 3.11.15 (the declared floor); the bcir-panels and torch-compiled-bf16 records name commit 5804ad5 (library 7a8a621fc181), the bcir-base records d5bc457 (library 8a7caca3a8db), each tree's runtime/c identical to its commit; indicative wall times, no PMU
reading: Median warm step, BCIR with the panels / PyTorch bf16 / BCIR before them: seed 1001 69.9 / 175.0 / 75.5 ms; seed 2002 69.1 / 147.1 / 75.8 ms; seed 3003 69.4 / 148.2 / 73.9 ms; seed 4004 69.0 / 150.9 / 75.4 ms; seed 20261011 68.6 / 170.5 / 72.2 ms (14,654-14,925 tokens a second with the panels, 13,500-14,180 before them, 5,853-6,963 for PyTorch). BCIR with the panels over PyTorch bf16 2.282 (95% interval 2.061-2.526, the first faster on 5 of 5), test cross-entropy difference +0.00054 nats (95% interval -0.00073 to +0.00181), inside the +-0.01 margin; BCIR with the panels over BCIR before them (what BF16-KERN and BF16-PANELS-1 buy) 1.078 (95% interval 1.054-1.102, the first faster on 5 of 5), test cross-entropy difference 0 (the same states); BCIR before them over PyTorch bf16 (LM-ATTN's pair, again in this session) 2.117 (95% interval 1.889-2.373, the first faster on 5 of 5), test cross-entropy difference +0.00054 nats, inside the margin. The two BCIR arms end in one state on 5 of 5 seeds (states_panels_as_base), and both in LM-ATTN's bcir-bf16-attn states on 5 of 5 (states_as_lm_attn): over 1,000 steps the commit changes no bit. The session ran slower than LM-ATTN's: the base arm's geometric mean step 74.6 ms against the same code's 70.9 there (x1.051), PyTorch's 157.9 against 142.9 (x1.105), so LM-ATTN's pair reads 2.117 here against 2.015 there -- the BCIR-to-PyTorch ratio moved about 5% between sessions by itself, and what BF16-KERN and BF16-PANELS-1 buy is the in-session 1.078. Peak RSS 534 MB for BCIR with the panels (they live in the binary32 slots: the arena the same 362,944,768 bytes and the workspace the same 11,534,592), 504-540 before them, 1,141-1,146 for PyTorch; the persistent state the same 157,390,848 bytes on every arm.

files.run.sh: the rounds as run (bash run.sh OUT TORCH_PYTHON HEAD_TREE BASE_TREE DATA_SRC from the repository root, the two trees worktrees of 5804ad5 and d5bc457, DATA_SRC LM-ATTN's prepared seeds: preparation is deterministic for a seed); a BCIR arm's record is removed before its run and a run that leaves none stops the rounds, since both BCIR arms write one record name
files.paired_panels.py, summary.json: the analysis fixed before the runs, and its output over runs/ (--previous LM-ATTN's summary.json, ../../attnfma/lm/summary.json)
files.runs/{bcir-panels,torch-compiled-bf16,bc: the fifteen train records (train_comparison.py's train stage): losses, gradient norms, every step's seconds, the evaluations, the final validation and test metrics, the state digest, peak RSS and the memory split
